$comment: Proving-performance regression baselines (GitHub #629; pairs with #534).
How to read / update this file:
- Stage numbers are the MEDIAN of 5 runs of CPU milliseconds (user+sys via
bash `time`), measured by scripts/perf/measure-proving.mjs on the GitHub
ubuntu-latest runner. CPU time is the gate metric because it is close to
deterministic across runner noise; wall medians are recorded too but only
informed the original numbers.
- The original baseline was established from the first dedicated runs of the
proving-perf workflow. To refresh after an intentional change (toolchain
bump, deliberate circuit growth), run the workflow on main and copy the
medians from the uploaded perf/proving-perf-report.json artifact into the
fields below, then note the reason in $history.
- witnessMs/proveMs gate with regressionThresholds.stageRatio (default 1.75x;
warn at ~1.3x). submitProxyMs and unknown stages are warn-only: the proxy
cannot see Soroban RPC, and missing data must not fake a green gate.
- ACIR opcode counts (the #534 pairing) gate at
regressionThresholds.gateRatio (default 1.15x) so circuit growth is
attributed independently of client-side slowdowns.
- provenance.bytecodeSha256 pins the compiled kyc_proof bytecode this
baseline was taken against, so a toolchain bump that changes codegen is
visible as a provenance mismatch (warn-only) rather than silently
re-baselining the clock.

kyc_proof.$comment: Matches circuits/AUDIT.md's committed nargo-info figure for kyc_proof (582 total ACIR opcodes). The workflow refreshes it from live measurement; drift vs AUDIT.md surfaces as a warning.

provenance.$comment2: bytecodeSha256 is filled on the first workflow run on main and committed; until then provenance checks are skipped (warn-only path).

$history.change: Initial gate established (issue #629). Stage numbers are provisional until the first measured runs on the fixed runner replace them; ACIR opcode count is the committed audit figure.
